AUTHORITY: PI 2026-09-12: 'Draft the opponent-channel ablation next. That is now the highest-value mechanism test... the stale-track result does not prove the policy ignores opponent position. It only shows that replacing current opponent positions with their t=0 positions did not produce a detectable absolute win-rate loss on these exploratory blocks. The clean next test is to destroy the opponent-position information rather than merely aging it.'
PURPOSE: Determine whether the frozen 6v6 specialists materially depend on opponent-position information at inference time.
MOTIVATED_BY_NOT_CONCLUDED_FROM: 6V6_TRACK_HOLD_DOSE_PILOT_V1 and 6V6_TRACK_HOLD_SEVERE_EXTENSION. Those showed no detectable absolute win-rate loss when opponent tracks were frozen at t=0, including at K=6 where z1 flipped 0 of 60 degraded episodes. That is suggestive but does NOT establish opponent-agnosticism: stale-at-t0 positions may remain accurate enough over these episode lengths, and the matchup may be winnable from geometry/flag state alone. This spec exists precisely because that inference was not licensed.

is_not: evidence that the policy is globally opponent-agnostic outside the tested observation channels and environment

WHERE_OPPONENT_POSITION_ACTUALLY_ENTERS_.path_1_grid: _build_grid_obs channel 2 -- _scatter_points(grid[:,i], 2, ex, ey, elive). Written through an alive/visibility mask; the grid is pre-zeroed, so elive=False leaves channel 2 empty. This IS the schema's native representation of 'no enemy information' (it is what sensor dropout / out-of-range already produce).
WHERE_OPPONENT_POSITION_ACTUALLY_ENTERS_.path_2_vec: _build_vec_obs feature 11 -- 'nearest enemy distance normalized to [0,1]', computed from enemy_x/enemy_y. NOTE: feature 11 does not consult enemy_alive at all; it mins over all enemy slots regardless of alive status.
WHERE_OPPONENT_POSITION_ACTUALLY_ENTERS_.no_other_path: every other vec feature is own-team, flag, mine, pickup, time, agent-id or score. _build_action_mask was previously audited and reads no enemy field, so action legality is unaffected.

global_state_checked_and_excluded.finding: build_global_state_batch (rl/global_state.py) DOES carry opponent information -- it reads core.red_x/red_y and derives red mean/std and carrier_enemy_nearest_dist features. If the actor consumed it, ablating grid+vec alone would leak and produce a spurious null.
global_state_checked_and_excluded.why_it_does_not_leak: rl/custom_ppo/policy.py::act() selects actions from self.policy_logits(obs, z_idx) masked by obs['mask']; global_state is used on the following line ONLY for self.values(...), the critic. The value head does not influence behaviour at inference.
global_state_checked_and_excluded.conclusion: at inference the opponent-information surface reaching the ACTION is exactly grid channel 2 and vec feature 11. The ablation is therefore complete for a win-rate outcome, and global_state is deliberately left untouched.
global_state_checked_and_excluded.caveat_if_ever_reused: this argument holds for inference-time action selection only. Any training-time use of this hook would also have to address the critic's global-state channel.

WHERE_OPPONENT_POSITION_ACTUALLY_ENTERS_.enemy_flag_deliberately_NOT_ablated: features 4-5 use enemy_flag, which is the objective's location, not an opponent agent position. Ablating it would confound 'opponent awareness' with 'objective awareness'. Scope decision, recorded.

WHAT_NEUTRAL_MEANS_AND_WHY_NOT_ZERO.critical: Naive 'set the opponent features to zero' would set vec feature 11 to 0.0, which in this schema means AN ENEMY IS AT ZERO DISTANCE -- maximally alarming, the opposite of absent. That would inject a large spurious effect and invalidate the experiment.
WHAT_NEUTRAL_MEANS_AND_WHY_NOT_ZERO.schema_convention_for_absent_objects: features 16 (nearest pickup) and 17 (nearest friendly mine) set distance to max_dist, normalising to 1.0, when the object mask is inactive.

therefore_ZERO_OPP_is.grid_channel_2: empty (elive forced False) -- the schema's own 'no enemy observed' encoding
therefore_ZERO_OPP_is.vec_feature_11: 1.0 (max normalised distance) -- matching the schema's absent-object convention

CONDITIONS.ZERO_OPP: opponent-position information removed as defined above (grid channel 2 empty; vec feature 11 = 1.0). No other field altered.
CONDITIONS.RANDOM_OPP: enemy_x/enemy_y replaced with uniform-random VALID map positions, refreshed at every observation, then the normal pipeline computes channel 2 and feature 11 from them. Randomisation is in-support by construction because it is drawn within map bounds and passed through the unmodified builders.

RANDOM_OPP_ONE_SET_PER_OBSERVATION_CYCLE.decision_frozen_before_running: ONE synthetic opponent set is drawn per observation cycle and BOTH the grid scatter (channel 2) and the nearest-enemy distance (vec 11) are derived from that same set.
RANDOM_OPP_ONE_SET_PER_OBSERVATION_CYCLE.why: _build_grid_obs and _build_vec_obs each call _side_tensors independently. Drawing fresh randoms per call would have scattered the grid at one set of positions while computing nearest-enemy distance from a DIFFERENT set -- the two channels would describe different worlds and the condition would be uninterpretable.
RANDOM_OPP_ONE_SET_PER_OBSERVATION_CYCLE.implementation: the draw is cached and the cache is cleared at the start of each get_obs_tensors call, so 'refreshed at every observation' holds while intra-observation consistency is guaranteed
RANDOM_OPP_ONE_SET_PER_OBSERVATION_CYCLE.verified_by_self_test: the differential self-test recomputes nearest-enemy distance from the cached synthetic positions and asserts it reproduces vec[11] to 1e-5; a mismatch fails closed

PERMUTE_OPP_DROPPED.status: NOT RUN -- provably vacuous in this observation schema
PERMUTE_OPP_DROPPED.proof: channel 2 is written by _scatter_points (a set scatter, order-invariant) and feature 11 is a min over enemy slots (symmetric). The observation contains no per-opponent identity anywhere. Permuting opponent identities therefore cannot change a single input value. Running it would spend seeds to measure an identity guaranteed by construction.
PERMUTE_OPP_DROPPED.note: this also means the policy CANNOT condition on opponent identity, only on the set of opponent positions -- itself a fact worth recording

INTEGRITY_REQUIREMENTS.observation_side_only: world truth, rewards, termination, legality masks, mines, flags and all non-opponent features unchanged
INTEGRITY_REQUIREMENTS.hook_gating: the substitution is raised ONLY inside _build_grid_obs and _build_vec_obs. _side_tensors is also called by _mines.py and _rules.py; a blanket patch would corrupt mine mechanics and win determination, as established during the track-hold implementation.
INTEGRITY_REQUIREMENTS.must_not_touch_env_rng: the env's native sensor model (rt_sensor_dropout_prob) draws from the env RNG via torch.rand(generator=self._rng). Using it would desync ablated episodes from FULL and destroy pairing. RANDOM_OPP therefore uses a SEPARATE numpy Generator seeded deterministically per (seed, condition), leaving the env RNG stream untouched.
INTEGRITY_REQUIREMENTS.self_test_required: before any pilot seed, verify that between FULL and each ablated condition ONLY the intended fields differ: grid channel 2 and vec feature 11 change, every other grid channel and every other vec feature are bit-identical, and core.red_x/red_y (world truth) are untouched.

POLICIES.why_specialists_first: the acquisition failure occurs BEFORE distillation. If pi_A and pi_B themselves barely react to destroying opponent-position information, that is directly relevant to why 6v6 strategy acquisition failed.
POLICIES.secondary_optional: Share-Encoder z0/z1 -- deferred, not run under this spec

SEEDS.why_shared: FULL, ZERO_OPP and RANDOM_OPP must be paired within seed so L is a within-episode contrast, not a different episode draw
SEEDS.disjointness_verified: grep for 17400001/17400032 across artifacts/**/*.json at freeze time: ZERO hits

DESIGN.full_2x2: both policies x both poles, so the complete payoff matrix is measured under each condition
DESIGN.cells: 2 policies x 2 poles x 3 conditions x 32 seeds = 384 episodes
DESIGN.estimated_runtime: ~5-6 h at the observed 6v6 pace, subject to machine load
DESIGN.cross_regime_also_reported: opponent information may matter more off-regime
DESIGN.delta_caveat: delta_A/delta_B computable from the 2x2 under each condition are DESCRIPTIVE ONLY and are not a specialization claim under any condition

POWER_DISCLOSED_BEFORE_RUNNING: n=32 is a first mechanism screen sized to detect GROSS dependence (a drop of roughly 0.2 or more). It cannot resolve small effects. A null here is evidence against strong dependence, not proof of none.

PRECOMMITTED_INTERPRETATION.A_zero_and_random_both_cause_large_loss: the policy materially uses opponent-position information
PRECOMMITTED_INTERPRETATION.B_zero_small_loss_random_large_loss: the policy tolerates missing opponent information but is disrupted by misleading opponent information
PRECOMMITTED_INTERPRETATION.C_both_little_or_no_directional_loss: consistent with weak dependence on opponent-position channels IN THE TESTED SETTING. Do NOT claim the policy is fully opponent-agnostic -- other observation channels may encode opponent consequences indirectly (e.g. own-agent tagging, score, flag state).
PRECOMMITTED_INTERPRETATION.D_strong_flips_but_near_zero_aggregate_l: opponent information affects trajectories but not directionally enough to move aggregate win rate on this exploratory block

NOT_AUTHORIZED_BY_THIS_RECORD: extending n or adding conditions after viewing the result

SEQUENCE: 1. Freeze this spec (done, before any episode)
2. Implement the ablation hook + differential self-test
3. Dry-run: self-test proves only channel 2 and vec[11] differ, world truth untouched
5. Report per policy/pole/condition with paired CIs and flip counts; branch per PRECOMMITTED_INTERPRETATION
6. Any training intervention gets a new frozen spec
